Sandstone
Pinkishto whitish medium grained rock with a number of subvertical mud filled fractures contained in limonite stained short sections near the top of the hole.  Smallish clay intraclasts are faintly pink to whitish and occur at levels of 1-3 per metrelocally.  Bedding traces range from 68-88deg to the CA.
Rare silty beds to a few cm in thickness are fist noted at 67.4m, the next a true siltstone horizon at 118.4m.
A section of loose sandy material was recovered from 104.4-107.1m  Rock above and below is quite competent suggesting a possible zone of faulting however, no orientation can be determined.
There is a general progression to coarser grain sizes below about 120m, with local coarse grained beds 5-10cm in thickness often containing a few small pebbley grains to 2-4mm.
The final sand infilled near vertical fracture noted occurs at ~122m.
Pebbly cm to 3cm thick horizons become prevalent below ~205m; maximun grain size of the fine pebbles to 7-8mm were noted near 215m and 220m.  Also short 5-15cm intensely hematitic intervals of purplish colour comprise a few percent of the length from 211-225m.  Fine pebbles comprise 3-5% of the unit below 215m, reaching concentrations of 7-8% over 5-30cm core lengths.
Silty beds ~ 2cm thick occur at 208.8m, 215.75m, 220.15m, and 232.8m, all at very high angle to the CA.  The final purplish hematitic layer noted for som distance occurs over 8-10cm at 228.5m.
Below 251m the Sandstone exhibits a bleached rather bright whitish colur and becomes weak to crumbly.  Recovery is poor and consists largely of rubble and loose sand from 251-278m. Due to the nature of recovered material it is impossible to determine precisely where losses occurred.
